newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on harvest, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on harvest, fund selling.

text.p: Forecasts for an active harvest weekend and aggressive fund selling tied to long liquidation amid a bearish technical picture knocked CBOT soybean futures to a sharply lower close, traders said.

"Technicals have dominated all week. The inability of the market to bounce was due to the clear harvest weekend," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "There was some light pre-hedging in beans but most farmers are busy with fieldwork and not marketing at all at these prices." Warm, dry weather over the weekend should ensure active harvesting of corn and soybeans in the U.S. Midwest, meteorologists said.
Traders also said a soybean production estimate from Sparks Companies was neutral to bearish.
Industry sources said the Memphis-based analytical firm estimated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.310 billion bushels, above USDA's September outlook for 2.270 billion.
Fund long liquidation weighed on prices with nearby November falling to a session low of $7.25-3/4 per bushel, the lowest level since $7.18-1/4 was touched on August 5.
Soybeans closed 8-3/4 to 11 cents per bushel lower, with November down 10-1/4 at $7.27-1/4. January was down 11 at $7.35-3/4.
November closed technically oversold with the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for that month at 17.554. Traders generally consider an RSI of 20 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
November broke below support at $7.32-3/4 and sell stops were hit with funds selling at least 25 million bushels, the traders said.
Merrill Lynch Futures, Smith Barney and Refco Inc each sold between eight and 10 million bushels of November, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 70,0000, down from 74,623 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services bought 400 January $7.75 calls at 10-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 2,500 January $7.50 puts and sold 2,500 January $7.25 puts at 14 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 32,000 contracts, down from 37,090 Thursday.
